Your First Bike Tour: Beginner Checklist

Every experienced tourer started exactly where you are now. Follow this timeline to ensure your first tour goes smoothly. One Week Before

  • Check tyre condition and pressures
  • Service bike or check oil and coolant
  • Test all electrics and lights
  • Plan route with fuel stops
  • Book accommodation
  • Check weather forecast
  • Download offline maps

One Day Before

  • Pack luggage using packing list
  • Do a loaded test ride
  • Charge all electronics
  • Check breakdown cover is active
  • Share route with someone at home
  • Fill fuel tank

On the Day

  • POWDDERS pre-ride check
  • Set sat nav before mounting
  • Adjust mirrors for loaded weight
  • Stop every 90 minutes minimum
  • Enjoy every mile!
keyTakeaways: The checklist splits preparation into one week before, one day before and the day itself.
A week ahead, check tyres, service the bike, plan your route and book accommodation.
The day before, pack using a list, do a loaded test ride and share your route with someone.
On the day, run a POWDDERS check and set your sat nav before you set off.
Stop at least every 90 minutes to stay fresh and enjoy the ride.

faq.q: How do I prepare for my first motorcycle tour?
faq.a: Work backwards from departure. A week before, check tyres and fluids or service the bike, plan your route with fuel stops, book accommodation and download offline maps. The day before, pack, do a loaded test ride and share your route. On the day, run a POWDDERS check, set your sat nav and set off unhurried.

faq.q: Why should I do a loaded test ride before a tour?
faq.a: A fully loaded bike handles differently, with more weight affecting braking, cornering and low-speed balance. A short test ride the day before lets you feel how the bike behaves with luggage and a full tank, adjust your mirrors and suspension if needed, and confirm everything is secured, so there are no surprises once the tour begins.

faq.q: How often should I stop on a touring day?
faq.a: Aim to stop at least every 90 minutes. Regular breaks keep you fresh, combat fatigue and concentration lapses, and let you rehydrate, stretch and check the bike over. On your first tour especially, resist the urge to push on for hours; frequent short stops make the day safer and more enjoyable.

faq.q: What should I check the week before departure?
faq.a: A week out gives time to fix anything you find. Check tyre condition and pressures, service the bike or check oil and coolant, test all electrics and lights, plan your route with fuel stops, book accommodation, check the weather forecast and download offline maps. Doing this early avoids a last-minute panic if something needs attention.

faq.q: Should I tell someone my route before setting off?
faq.a: Yes. Sharing your planned route and expected arrival times with someone at home is a simple safety net. If you break down in a remote area with no signal or have an accident, they know roughly where to look and can raise the alarm. Confirm your breakdown cover is active before you leave as well.
